subject.title: Import Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter captures into the canonical local store

question: Should Birdclaw adopt versioned third-party passive-capture exports as a supported core ingestion surface, and if so should the initial contract cover only Scrollmark canonical bundle v1?
rationale: This choice creates a durable compatibility and attribution contract for externally controlled schemas; source inspection can identify an implementation path but cannot determine the permanent product support boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrow v1 adapter
options.body: Support only validated Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 initially, with explicit provenance, partial-collection semantics, backup coverage, and no legacy auto-detection until separate evidence supports it.

options.title: Approve multiple producers now
options.body: Define and implement separate versioned adapters for Scrollmark legacy exports and twitter-web-exporter alongside canonical bundle v1, accepting a larger initial compatibility surface.

options.title: Defer external capture imports
options.body: Keep archive and live transports as the only supported ingestion sources until third-party schemas demonstrate longer-term stability or stronger user demand.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow v1 adapter
recommendation.body: Support only validated Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 initially, with explicit provenance, partial-collection semantics, backup coverage, and no legacy auto-detection until separate evidence supports it.
